sections.title: Types and methods of data transmission
The internet and the world wide web

items.text: Understand how and why computers use binary to represent all forms of data
keys: computers use binary to represent all forms of data
notes: Any form of data needs to be converted to binary to be processed by a computer
Data is processed using logic gates and stored in registers
items.detail: Core idea: all forms of data must be represented in binary so the computer can process them. In the syllabus, processing is carried out using logic gates and data is stored in registers.
items.svg: Why binary is used

items.text: Understand the denary, binary and hexadecimal number systems, and convert between positive denary, positive binary and positive hexadecimal
keys: denary, binary and hexadecimal number systems
positive denary, positive binary and positive hexadecimal
notes: Denary is a base 10 system · Binary is a base 2 system · Hexadecimal is a base 16 system
Values used will be integers only
Conversions go in both directions, e.g. denary → binary or binary → denary
Maximum binary number length of 16-bit
items.detail:
Three number systems: denary = base 10; binary = base 2; hexadecimal = base 16. You must convert between positive denary, positive binary and positive hexadecimal. Values are integers, with binary values limited to 16 bits.

Binary ↔ hexadecimal
BinaryHex
00000
10019
1111F

One hexadecimal digit represents exactly four binary bits, so split a binary value into groups of four.

items.text: Understand how and why hexadecimal is used as a beneficial method of data representation
keys: hexadecimal is used as a beneficial method of data representation
notes: Areas within computer science that hexadecimal is used should be identified
Hexadecimal is easier for humans to understand than binary, as it is a shorter representation of binary
items.detail: Why hexadecimal is useful: it is a shorter representation of binary and therefore easier for humans to read and work with. You should be able to identify areas of computer science where hexadecimal is used.

items.text: Add two positive 8-bit binary integers, and understand the concept of overflow and why it occurs in binary addition
notes: An overflow error will occur if the value is greater than 255 in an 8-bit register
A computer or device has a predefined limit that it can represent or store, for example 16-bit
An overflow error occurs when a value outside this limit should be returned
items.detail:
8-bit positive range: 00000000 to 11111111 = 0 to 255. Overflow occurs when the result is outside the fixed number of bits available.

Overflow check
8-bit register → maximum 255 → result > 255 → overflow

items.text: Perform a logical binary shift on a positive 8-bit binary integer, and understand the effect this has on the value
keys: the effect this has on the value
notes: Perform logical left shifts · logical right shifts · multiple shifts
Bits shifted off the end of the register are lost, and zeros are shifted in at the opposite end
The value is multiplied or divided according to the shift performed
The most significant bit(s) or least significant bit(s) are lost
items.detail:
OperationEffect
Logical left shiftBits move left; zeroes enter from the right; bits shifted out are lost.
Logical right shiftBits move right; zeroes enter from the left; bits shifted out are lost.

The value changes by a factor of 2 for each place shifted, subject to bits being lost.

Exam trap: a left shift that pushes a 1 out of the MSB gives a wrong value; a right shift discards the LSBs, so the division is truncated.
items.svg: Logical shifts on one byte

items.text: Use the two's complement number system to represent positive and negative 8-bit binary integers
notes: Convert a positive binary or denary integer to a two's complement 8-bit integer and vice versa
Convert a negative binary or denary integer to a two's complement 8-bit integer and vice versa
items.detail:
8-bit two’s complement
Bit weights−128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1
Range−128 to +127

For a negative value: write the positive binary value, invert the bits, then add 1.

Smallest value −128 = 1000 0000; largest +127 = 0111 1111. If the MSB is 1, the number is negative.
items.svg: Two’s complement: +45 → −45

items.text: Understand how and why a computer represents text and the use of character sets, including ASCII and Unicode
notes: Text is converted to binary to be processed by a computer
Unicode allows for a greater range of characters and symbols than ASCII, including different languages and emojis
Unicode requires more bits per character than ASCII
items.detail:
Character setWhat to know
ASCIIRepresents characters using a smaller set of character codes.
UnicodeRepresents a much larger range of characters and symbols, including different languages and emojis.

In both cases, character codes are represented in binary for processing.
items.svg:
Character set: each character has a code
CharacterASCII (denary)Binary
space320010 0000
0480011 0000
A650100 0001
a970110 0001

Codes are consecutive: B = 66, C = 67 … b = 98. Unicode uses more bits per character, so it covers many more languages and symbols.

items.text: Understand how and why a computer represents sound, including the effects of the sample rate and sample resolution
keys: effects of the sample rate and sample resolution
notes: A sound wave is sampled so it can be converted to binary for a computer to process
The sample rate is the number of samples taken per second
The sample resolution is the number of bits used per sample
Recording accuracy and file size both increase as sample rate and resolution increase

items.text: Understand how and why a computer represents an image, including the effects of the resolution and colour depth
keys: effects of the resolution and colour depth
notes: An image is a series of pixels, converted to binary, that a computer processes
The resolution is the number of pixels in the image
The colour depth is the number of bits used to represent each pixel's colour
File size and image quality both increase as resolution and colour depth increase
items.detail:
Resolution = number of pixels

8 × 8

16 × 16

Higher resolution means more pixels in the image. Higher colour depth means more bits are used for each colour.

Exam relationship: increasing resolution or colour depth increases both image file size and image quality.
items.svg: Image representation: resolution and colour depth

items.text: Understand how data storage is measured
notes: Includes: bit, nibble, byte, kibibyte (KiB), mebibyte (MiB), gibibyte (GiB), tebibyte (TiB), pebibyte (PiB), exbibyte (EiB)
Each unit holds a fixed amount of the previous one, e.g. 8 bits in a byte, 1024 mebibytes in a gibibyte
items.detail:
UnitRelationship
bitsingle 0 or 1
nibble4 bits
byte8 bits
KiB1024 bytes
MiB1024 KiB
GiB1024 MiB
TiB1024 GiB
PiB1024 TiB
EiB1024 PiB
items.svg: Storage units: bit → byte → KiB … EiB

items.text: Calculate the file size of an image file and a sound file, using information given
keys: file size of an image file and a sound file
notes: Give answers in the units specified in the question
Calculations must use 1024, not 1000
Information given may include image resolution and colour depth, or sound sample rate, resolution and length of track
items.detail:
File typeCalculation
Imagewidth × height × colour depth = bits
Soundsample rate × sample resolution × length = bits

Convert bits to bytes by dividing by 8, then convert to the requested storage unit using 1024.
items.svg: Size calculation chain with worked examples

items.text: Understand the purpose of and need for data compression
keys: purpose of and need for data compression
notes: Compression exists to reduce the size of a file
Impact: less bandwidth required, less storage space required, shorter transmission time
items.detail: Purpose: reduce file size. The syllabus links this to less bandwidth required, less storage space required and shorter transmission time.

items.text: Understand how files are compressed using lossy and lossless compression methods
notes: Lossy compression reduces file size by permanently removing data, e.g. reducing resolution/colour depth, or sample rate/resolution
Lossless compression reduces file size without permanently losing any data, e.g. run length encoding (RLE)
items.detail:
LossyLossless
Some data is permanently removed.No data is permanently lost.
Used when reducing file size can justify loss of data.Data can be recovered without loss.
Examples in the syllabus include reducing resolution/colour depth or sample rate/resolution.Example: run length encoding (RLE).

items.text: Understand that data is broken down into packets to be transmitted, and describe the structure of a packet
notes: A packet contains a packet header, payload and trailer
The packet header includes the destination address, packet number and originator's address
items.detail:
Packet structure — learn these three parts
Header
destination address
packet number
originator’s address
Payload
data being transmitted
Trailer
error-check data

Exam trap: do not omit any of Header, Payload and Trailer when asked to describe the structure.
items.svg: Packet structure

items.text: Describe the process of packet switching
notes: Data is broken down into packets
Each packet could take a different route
A router controls the route a packet takes
Packets may arrive out of order
Once the last packet has arrived, packets are reordered
items.detail:
Packet switching sequence
1Data is broken down into packets
2Each packet can take a different route
3A router controls the route of each packet
4Packets may arrive out of order
5The packets are reordered after all have arrived
items.svg: Packet switching: packets can use different routes

items.text: Describe how data is transmitted using different methods of data transmission, and explain the suitability of each method for a given scenario
keys: suitability of each method for a given scenario
notes: Includes serial, parallel, simplex, half-duplex and full-duplex
Includes the advantages and disadvantages of each method
items.detail:
MethodCore feature to know
SerialData is transmitted one bit at a time.
ParallelMultiple bits are transmitted at the same time.
SimplexData travels in one direction only.
Half-duplexBoth directions are possible, but not at the same time.
Full-duplexBoth directions are possible at the same time.

For scenario questions, select the method whose advantages and disadvantages suit the stated situation.
items.svg: Transmission methods at a glance

items.text: Understand the universal serial bus (USB) interface and explain how it is used to transmit data
notes: Includes the benefits and drawbacks of the interface
items.detail:
USB pointWhat the syllabus expects
InterfaceUniversal Serial Bus used to transmit data.
Advantages / drawbacksKnow the benefits and drawbacks of using the interface.

items.text: Understand the need to check for errors after data transmission and how these errors can occur
notes: Errors can occur during data transmission due to interference, e.g. data loss, data gain and data change
items.detail: Why check? Transmission can cause data loss, data gain or data change because of interference. Error detection methods allow the receiver/sender to identify that the received data is not correct.

items.text: Describe the processes involved in each of the following error detection methods: parity check (odd and even), checksum and echo check
keys: parity check (odd and even), checksum and echo check
notes: Includes parity byte and parity block check
items.detail:
MethodProcess
Parity checkAdd a parity bit so the number of 1s is odd or even, then check the received data.
ChecksumCalculate a value from the data, transmit it, recalculate it at the receiver and compare.
Echo checkSend the received data back to the sender, which compares it with the original.

The syllabus also includes parity byte and parity block check.

MethodStrengthWeakness
Parity checkSimple, fastOnly detects odd-bit errors
ChecksumDetects burst errorsCan miss some errors
Echo checkConfirms exact matchHigh overhead, slow
items.svg: Block parity: finding the corrupted bit

items.text: Describe how a check digit is used to detect errors in data entry, and identify examples of when a check digit is used, including ISBNs and bar codes
items.detail:
Check digit: an extra digit in a data code, calculated from the other digits. Recalculate the check digit when the data is entered and compare the result. A mismatch indicates an error.

Examples required: ISBNs and bar codes.

items.text: Describe how an automatic repeat query (ARQ) can be used to establish that data is received without error
notes: Includes the use of positive/negative acknowledgements, and timeout
items.detail:
ARQ
1Sender transmits data
2Receiver sends a positive acknowledgement if correct
3Receiver sends a negative acknowledgement if incorrect
4If no acknowledgement arrives before timeout, the sender resends

ARQ uses an acknowledgement and timeout to decide whether the data needs to be resent.
items.svg: ARQ

items.text: Understand the need for and purpose of encryption when transmitting data
items.detail: Purpose: encryption protects data during transmission by making it unreadable without the appropriate method/key for decryption.

items.text: Understand how data is encrypted using symmetric and asymmetric encryption
notes: Asymmetric encryption includes the use of public and private keys
items.detail:
SymmetricAsymmetric
Uses the same key for encryption and decryption.Uses a public key and private key.

Know the distinction between these two methods and the role of the public/private keys in asymmetric encryption.
items.svg: Encryption methods: the key idea

items.text: Understand the role of the central processing unit (CPU) in a computer, and what is meant by a microprocessor
notes: The CPU processes instructions and data that are input into the computer so that the result can be output
A microprocessor is a type of integrated circuit on a single chip
items.detail:
TermDefinition
CPUProcesses instructions and data input into the computer so a result can be output.
MicroprocessorA type of integrated circuit on a single chip.

items.text: Understand the purpose of the components in a CPU with Von Neumann architecture, and describe the fetch–decode–execute (FDE) cycle
notes: Includes units: arithmetic logic unit (ALU) and control unit (CU)
Includes registers: program counter (PC), memory address register (MAR), memory data register (MDR), current instruction register (CIR) and accumulator (ACC)
Includes buses: address bus, data bus and control bus
items.detail:
Von Neumann CPU — components to recognise
Unit / register / busRole in the syllabus
ALUArithmetic and logic operations.
CUControls the operation of the CPU.
PCHolds the address of the next instruction.
MARHolds the address to be accessed.
MDRHolds data being transferred.
CIRHolds the current instruction.
ACCStores intermediate calculation results.
Address busTransmits addresses.
Data busTransmits data.
Control busTransmits control signals.
FDE cycle
Fetch → Decode → Execute → repeat
items.svg: CPU: main components and registers

items.text: Understand what is meant by a core, cache and clock in a CPU, and explain how they can affect the performance of a CPU
keys: affect the performance of a CPU
notes: The number of cores, size of the cache and speed of the clock can all affect the performance of a CPU
items.detail:
FeaturePerformance link
Number of coresCan affect CPU performance.
Cache sizeCan affect CPU performance.
Clock speedCan affect CPU performance.

items.text: Understand the purpose and use of an instruction set for a CPU
notes: An instruction set is a list of all the commands that can be processed by a CPU, and the commands are machine code
items.detail: An instruction set is the list of commands a CPU can process. These commands are machine code.

items.text: Describe the purpose and characteristics of an embedded system, and identify devices in which they are commonly used
notes: An embedded system is used to perform a dedicated function, e.g. in domestic appliances, cars, security systems, lighting systems or vending machines
Different from a general purpose computer (e.g. a PC or laptop) that performs many functions
items.detail:
Embedded systemGeneral purpose computer
Designed for a dedicated function.Designed to perform many different functions.
Common uses in the syllabus: domestic appliances, cars, security systems, lighting systems, vending machines.Example in the syllabus: PC or laptop.

items.text: Understand what is meant by an input device and why it is required
notes: Includes: barcode scanner, digital camera, keyboard, microphone, optical mouse, QR code scanner, touch screen (resistive, capacitive, infra-red), 2D and 3D scanners
items.detail: Input device: a device used to enter data into a computer. Know the syllabus list: barcode scanner, digital camera, keyboard, microphone, optical mouse, QR code scanner, touch screen (resistive, capacitive, infra-red), 2D scanner and 3D scanner.

items.text: Understand what is meant by an output device and why it is required
notes: Includes: actuator, digital light processing (DLP) projector, inkjet printer, laser printer, LED screen, LCD projector, LCD screen, speaker, 3D printer
items.detail: Output device: a device that provides output from the computer. Know the syllabus list: actuator, DLP projector, inkjet printer, laser printer, LED screen, LCD projector, LCD screen, speaker and 3D printer.

items.text: Understand what is meant by a sensor and the purposes of sensors, and identify the type of data captured by each sensor and when each would be used
keys: type of data captured by each sensor
notes: Limited to: acoustic, accelerometer, flow, gas, humidity, infra-red, level, light, magnetic field, moisture, pH, pressure, proximity, temperature
items.detail:
SensorData captured / typical use
AcousticSound level.
AccelerometerAcceleration / movement.
FlowFlow rate.
GasGas concentration.
HumidityHumidity level.
Infra-redInfra-red radiation / detection.
LevelLevel of a substance.
LightLight level.
Magnetic fieldMagnetic field strength.
MoistureMoisture level.
pHAcidity/alkalinity.
PressurePressure.
ProximityCloseness to an object.
TemperatureTemperature.
items.svg: Automated system: sensor → processing → action

items.text: Understand what is meant by primary storage
notes: Primary storage is directly accessed by the CPU
Includes the role of random access memory (RAM) and read only memory (ROM)
Includes why a computer needs both RAM and ROM, and the difference between them
items.detail:
RAMROM
Primary storage; contents can change while the computer is running.Primary storage; contents are read-only in normal use.
Used for data/instructions needed during operation.Provides stored instructions/data that must be retained.

Primary storage is directly accessed by the CPU; the syllabus requires knowing why both RAM and ROM are needed.

items.text: Understand what is meant by secondary storage
notes: Secondary storage is not directly accessed by the CPU and is necessary for more permanent storage of data
items.detail: Secondary storage is not directly accessed by the CPU and provides more permanent storage of data.

items.text: Describe the operation of magnetic, optical and solid-state (flash memory) storage, and give examples of each
keys: magnetic, optical and solid-state (flash memory) storage
items.detail:
Storage typeOperationExample required
MagneticUses platters divided into tracks and sectors; data is read and written using electromagnets.Hard disk drive (HDD)
OpticalUses lasers to create and read pits and lands.CD / DVD / Blu-ray
Solid-state (flash)Uses NAND or NOR technology; transistors are used as control gates and floating gates.Solid-state drive (SSD) / SD card / USB drive

items.text: Describe what is meant by virtual memory, how it is created and used, and why it is necessary
notes: Pages of data are transferred between RAM and virtual memory when needed
items.detail:
Virtual memory
RAM ↔ pages of data ↔ virtual memory

Pages of data are transferred between RAM and virtual memory when needed. Virtual memory is used when more memory is needed than is currently available in RAM.

items.text: Understand what is meant by cloud storage
notes: Cloud storage can be accessed remotely, compared to storing data locally
items.detail: Cloud storage means data is stored remotely and accessed over a network rather than being stored only on the local device.

items.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of storing data on the cloud in comparison to storing it locally
notes: Physical servers and storage are still needed somewhere to store data in cloud storage
items.detail:
Cloud storageLocal storage
Can be accessed remotely.Stored on the local device.
Physical servers/storage are still required somewhere to hold the data.Does not require remote access to retrieve the locally stored data.

items.text: Understand that a computer needs a network interface card (NIC) to access a network
items.detail:
A network interface card (NIC) is required for a computer to access a network.

The NIC is the hardware that connects a device to a network, wired or wireless.

items.text: Understand what is meant by, and the purpose of, a media access control (MAC) address, including its structure
notes: A NIC is given a MAC address at the point of manufacture
MAC addresses are usually written as hexadecimal
MAC addresses are created using the manufacturer code and the serial code
items.detail: MAC address: the address given to a NIC at manufacture. It is usually written in hexadecimal and is created using the manufacturer code and serial code.

items.text: Understand what is meant by, and the purpose of, an internet protocol (IP) address, and that there are different types of IP address
notes: An IP address is allocated by the network and can be static or dynamic
Includes the characteristics of, and differences between, IPv4 and IPv6
items.detail:
IP addressWhat to know
PurposeAn address allocated by the network.
TypesStatic or dynamic.
IPv4 / IPv6Know their characteristics and the differences between them.

items.text: Describe the role of a router in a network
notes: A router sends data to a specific destination on a network
A router can assign IP addresses
A router can connect a local network to the internet
items.detail: Router: sends data to a specific destination on a network, can assign IP addresses and can connect a local network to the internet.
items.svg: NIC, MAC address, router and IP address

items.text: Describe the difference between system software and application software, and provide examples of each
notes: System software provides the services that the computer requires, including operating system and utility software
Application software provides the services that the user requires
items.detail:
System softwareApplication software
Provides services required by the computer, including the operating system and utility software.Provides services required by the user.

items.text: Describe the role and basic functions of an operating system
notes: Includes: managing files, handling interrupts, providing an interface, managing peripherals and drivers, managing memory, managing multitasking, providing a platform for running applications, providing system security, managing user accounts
items.detail:
Operating system functions to know:

  • managing files
  • handling interrupts
  • providing an interface
  • managing peripherals and drivers
  • managing memory
  • managing multitasking
  • providing a platform for applications
  • providing system security
  • managing user accounts

items.text: Understand how hardware, firmware and an operating system are required to run applications software
keys: hardware, firmware and an operating system
items.detail: Application software depends on the underlying hardware, firmware and operating system to run.
items.svg: Interrupt handling sequence

items.text: Describe the role and operation of interrupts
notes: Includes how an interrupt is generated, how it is handled using an interrupt service routine, and what happens as a result
Software interrupts include division by zero and two processes trying to access the same memory location
Hardware interrupts include pressing a key on the keyboard and moving the mouse
items.detail:
Interrupt handling
1An interrupt is generated
2The operating system responds by running the interrupt service routine
3The interrupt is handled and the required action occurs
4Normal processing resumes
TypeSyllabus examples
Software interruptDivision by zero; two processes trying to access the same memory location.
Hardware interruptPressing a keyboard key; moving the mouse.

items.text: Explain what is meant by a high-level language and a low-level language, including the advantages and disadvantages of each
keys: high-level language and a low-level language
notes: Includes ease of reading/writing code, ease of debugging code, machine independence, direct manipulation of hardware
items.detail:
High-levelLow-level
Generally easier to read and write.Closer to the hardware.
Generally easier to debug.Allows direct manipulation of hardware.
More machine independent.More machine dependent.

These comparisons are the specific advantages/disadvantages required by the syllabus.

items.text: Understand that assembly language is a form of low-level language that uses mnemonics, and that an assembler is needed to translate an assembly language program into machine code
items.detail: Assembly language is a low-level language that uses mnemonics. An assembler translates an assembly-language program into machine code.

items.text: Describe the operation of a compiler and an interpreter, including how high-level language is translated by each and how errors are reported
notes: A compiler translates the whole code at once before executing it, producing an executable file
An interpreter translates and executes the code line-by-line
A compiler provides an error report for the whole code if errors are detected; an interpreter stops execution when an error is found
items.detail:
CompilerInterpreter
Translates the whole code before execution and produces an executable file.Translates and executes code line by line.
Reports errors for the whole code if errors are detected.Stops execution when an error is found.
items.svg: Compiler vs interpreter

items.text: Explain the advantages and disadvantages of a compiler and an interpreter
notes: An interpreter is mostly used when developing a program; a compiler is used to translate the finished program
items.detail: Use in the development process: an interpreter is mostly used during development; a compiler is used to translate the finished program.

items.text: Explain the role of an IDE in writing program code, and the common functions IDEs provide
notes: Includes: code editors, run-time environment, translators, error diagnostics, auto-completion, auto-correction, prettyprint
items.detail:
IDE functionWhat it provides
Code editorWrite and edit program code.
Run-time environmentRun the program.
TranslatorTranslate program code.
Error diagnosticsHelp identify errors.
Auto-completionComplete code as it is written.
Auto-correctionCorrect certain coding issues automatically.
PrettyprintFormat code to improve readability.

items.text: Understand the difference between the internet and the world wide web
keys: the internet and the world wide web
notes: The internet is the infrastructure
The world wide web is the collection of websites and web pages accessed using the internet
items.detail:
InternetWorld Wide Web
The infrastructure.The collection of websites and web pages accessed using the internet.

items.text: Understand what is meant by a uniform resource locator (URL)
notes: A URL is a text-based address for a web page; it can contain the protocol, the domain name and the web page/file name
items.detail: A URL is a text-based address for a web page. It can contain the protocol, domain name and web page/file name.

items.text: Describe the purpose and operation of hypertext transfer protocol (HTTP) and hypertext transfer protocol secure (HTTPS)
keys: hypertext transfer protocol (HTTP) and hypertext transfer protocol secure (HTTPS)
items.detail:
HTTPHTTPS
Protocol used for transferring web pages/data.Secure form of HTTP used when transmitting web data.

items.text: Explain the purpose and functions of a web browser
notes: The main purpose of a web browser is to render hypertext markup language (HTML) and display web pages
Functions include: storing bookmarks and favourites, recording user history, allowing use of multiple tabs, storing cookies, providing navigation tools, providing an address bar
items.detail: Browser purpose: render HTML and display web pages. Functions required by the syllabus include bookmarks/favourites, history, multiple tabs, cookies, navigation tools and an address bar.

items.text: Describe how web pages are located, retrieved and displayed on a device when a user enters a URL
keys: located, retrieved and displayed on a device
notes: Includes the role of: the web browser, IP addresses, the domain name server (DNS), the web server, HTML
items.detail:
URL → page
1Browser receives the URL
2DNS is used to obtain the IP address
3The browser requests the page from the web server
4The web server returns the HTML
5The browser renders the HTML as the web page

Remember the chain: URL → DNS → IP address → web server → HTML → browser renders the page.
items.svg: When a user enters a URL

items.text: Explain what is meant by cookies and how they are used, including session cookies and persistent cookies
notes: Cookies are used for functions including: saving personal details, tracking user preferences, holding items in an online shopping cart, storing login details
items.detail:
Cookie typeWhat to know
Session cookieUsed for a browsing session and removed when the session ends.
Persistent cookieCan remain stored after the current session.

Uses in the syllabus include saving personal details, tracking preferences, holding online shopping cart items and storing login details.
items.svg: Cookie: how a website remembers you

items.text: Understand the concept of a digital currency and how digital currencies are used
notes: A digital currency is one that only exists electronically
items.detail: A digital currency exists only electronically. Know the concept and how digital currencies are used.

items.text: Understand the process of blockchain and how it is used to track digital currency transactions
notes: Blockchain, in its basic form, is a digital ledger, that is a time-stamped series of records that cannot be altered
items.detail:
Blockchain
time-stamped records → linked as a chain → digital ledger

The syllabus describes blockchain, in its basic form, as a digital ledger: a time-stamped series of records that cannot be altered, used to track digital currency transactions.
items.svg: Blockchain: blocks chained by hashes

items.text: Describe the processes involved in, and the aim of carrying out, a range of cyber security threats
keys: aim of carrying out, a range of cyber security threats
items.detail:
ThreatAim / process to know
Brute-force attackAttempts possible passwords/keys to gain access.
Data interceptionCaptures data while it is being transmitted.
DDoS attackFloods a service with requests so it cannot respond normally.
HackingAttempts unauthorised access.
MalwareIncludes virus, worm, Trojan horse, spyware, adware and ransomware.
PharmingRedirects a user to a fraudulent site.
PhishingUses deceptive communication to obtain information.
Social engineeringManipulates people to obtain information or access.

items.text: Explain how a range of solutions are used to help keep data safe from security threats
items.detail:
SolutionPurpose
Access levelsLimit what a user can access or change.
FirewallControls/filter network traffic.
Proxy serverActs as an intermediary for network requests.
Privacy settingsControl exposure of user information.
Anti-malwareHelps protect against malicious software.
AuthenticationConfirms a user’s identity.
Software updatesKeep software updated to address security weaknesses.
Human checksCheck spelling/tone and the URL to help identify phishing.
SSL security protocolHelps keep transmitted data secure.

items.text: Describe how sensors, microprocessors and actuators can be used in collaboration to create automated systems
items.detail:
Automated system
Sensor → Microprocessor → Actuator

The sensor captures data; the microprocessor processes the sensor data; the actuator carries out the required action.
items.svg: Automated system: decision loop

items.text: Describe the advantages and disadvantages of an automated system used for a given scenario
notes: Includes scenarios from: industry, transport, agriculture, weather, gaming, lighting, science
items.detail:
ScenarioWhat to compare
Industry / transport / agriculture / weather / gaming / lighting / scienceState advantages and disadvantages of the automated system in the given scenario.

items.text: Understand what is meant by robotics
notes: Robotics is a branch of computer science that incorporates the design, construction and operation of robots
Examples include factory equipment, domestic robots and drones
items.detail: Robotics is the branch of computer science that incorporates the design, construction and operation of robots. Syllabus examples include factory equipment, domestic robots and drones.

items.text: Describe the characteristics of a robot
notes: Includes: a mechanical structure or framework, electrical components such as sensors, microprocessors and actuators, and being programmable
items.detail:
• mechanical structure or framework
  • electrical components such as sensors, microprocessors and actuators
  • programmable

items.text: Understand the roles that robots can perform, and describe the advantages and disadvantages of their use
notes: Robots can be used in areas including: industry, transport, agriculture, medicine, domestic settings, entertainment
items.detail: Know the roles robots can perform and give advantages/disadvantages for the stated use. Syllabus areas include industry, transport, agriculture, medicine, domestic settings and entertainment.

items.text: Understand what is meant by artificial intelligence (AI)
notes: AI is a branch of computer science dealing with the simulation of intelligent behaviours by computers
items.detail: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a branch of computer science dealing with the simulation of intelligent behaviours by computers.

items.text: Describe the main characteristics of AI as the collection of data and the rules for using that data, the ability to reason, and it can include the ability to learn and adapt
keys: the collection of data and the rules for using that data, the ability to reason
the ability to learn and adapt
items.detail:
• collection of data
  • rules for using that data
  • ability to reason
  • can include the ability to learn and adapt

items.text: Explain the basic operation and components of AI systems to simulate intelligent behaviour
notes: Limited to: expert systems and machine learning
Expert systems have a knowledge base, a rule base, an inference engine and an interface
Machine learning is when a program has the ability to automatically adapt its own processes and/or data
items.detail:
Expert systemMachine learning
Knowledge base + rule base + inference engine + interface.A program can automatically adapt its own processes and/or data.
items.svg: AI systems: the two syllabus areas

items.text: Understand the program development life cycle, limited to: analysis, design, coding and testing
notes: Analysis: abstraction, decomposition of the problem, identification of the problem and requirements
Design: decomposition, structure diagrams, flowcharts, pseudocode
Coding: writing program code and iterative testing
Testing: testing program code with the use of test data
items.detail:
StageSyllabus content
AnalysisAbstraction, decomposition, identify problem and requirements.
DesignDecomposition, structure diagrams, flowcharts, pseudocode.
CodingWrite program code and test iteratively.
TestingTest program code using test data.
items.svg: Program development life cycle

items.text: Understand that every computer system is made up of sub-systems, understand how a problem can be decomposed into its component parts, and use different methods to design and construct a solution to a problem
keys: design and construct a solution to a problem
notes: Decomposition includes: inputs, processes, outputs, storage
Design methods include: structure diagrams, flowcharts, pseudocode
items.detail: Decomposition: break a problem/system into component parts or sub-systems. The syllabus identifies inputs, processes, outputs and storage. Design methods are structure diagrams, flowcharts and pseudocode.

items.text: Explain the purpose of a given algorithm
notes: Includes stating the purpose of an algorithm, and describing the processes involved in an algorithm
items.detail: When given an algorithm, identify the problem/result it is designed for and describe the processes it carries out.

items.text: Understand standard methods of solution, limited to: linear search, bubble sort, totalling, counting, finding maximum, minimum and average values
keys: linear search, bubble sort, totalling, counting, finding maximum, minimum and average values
items.detail:
MethodCore idea
Linear searchSearch through items sequentially.
Bubble sortRepeatedly compare and swap adjacent items.
TotallingAccumulate a total.
CountingAccumulate a count.
Maximum / minimumFind the largest / smallest value.
AverageFind the mean value.
items.svg: Bubble sort: one pass over [5, 3, 8, 1]

items.text: Understand the need for validation checks and verification checks to be made on input data, and the different types of each
notes: Validation includes: range check, length check, type check, presence check, format check, check digit
Verification includes: visual check, double entry check
items.detail:
ValidationVerification
Range, length, type, presence, format, check digit.Visual check, double entry check.
Checks whether data is acceptable according to rules.Checks whether data has been entered/copied correctly.
items.svg: Validation asks “acceptable?”; verification asks “correctly copied?”

items.text: Suggest and apply suitable test data, limited to: normal, abnormal, extreme and boundary
notes: Extreme data is the largest/smallest acceptable value
Boundary data is the largest/smallest acceptable value and the corresponding smallest/largest rejected value
items.detail:
Test dataMeaning
NormalTypical valid data.
AbnormalInvalid data that should be rejected.
ExtremeLargest/smallest acceptable value.
BoundaryLargest/smallest acceptable value and the corresponding smallest/largest rejected value.
items.svg: Boundary test data

items.text: Complete a trace table to document a dry-run of an algorithm
notes: Includes, at each step in an algorithm: variables, outputs, user prompts
items.detail: A trace table records the values at each step of a dry-run. Include variables, outputs and user prompts as required by the syllabus.
items.svg:
Dry-run: trace table for a short loop
total ← 0 FOR count ← 1 TO 3 total ← total + count OUTPUT total NEXT count
counttotalOUTPUT
—0
111
233
366

items.text: Identify errors in given algorithms and suggest ways of correcting these errors
items.detail: Read the given algorithm, identify where its logic is wrong, then state how the error can be corrected.

items.text: Write and amend algorithms for given problems or scenarios, using pseudocode, program code and flowcharts
notes: Precision is required when writing algorithms, e.g. x > y is acceptable but "x is greater than y" is not
items.detail: Write and amend algorithms using pseudocode, program code and flowcharts. Cambridge requires precision in the algorithm notation; use exact comparison operators and other syntax as required.

items.text: Declare and use variables and constants
items.detail:
VariableA named value that can change.
ConstantA named value that does not change during program execution.

DECLARE creates a variable with a data type; a constant keeps one value for the whole program.

DECLARE Score : INTEGER CONSTANT Pi ← 3.14

items.text: Understand and use basic data types
notes: Includes: integer, real, char, string, Boolean
items.detail:
TypeMeaning
INTEGERWhole number.
REALNumber that can contain a fractional part.
CHARSingle character.
STRINGSequence of characters.
BOOLEANTRUE or FALSE.

items.text: Understand and use input and output
items.detail:
INPUTReceives data into the program.
OUTPUTDisplays/sends data from the program.

INPUT reads a value from the user into a variable; OUTPUT displays a value or message. Show a prompt before INPUT.

items.text: Understand and use the concept of sequence
items.detail:
Sequence means program statements are executed in order.

Sequence = statements run one after another, in the order written. Changing the order changes the result.

items.text: Understand and use the concept of selection
notes: Includes IF statements and CASE statements
items.detail:
SelectionRequired forms
IFChoose between paths based on a condition.
CASEChoose between alternatives based on the value being tested.

items.text: Understand and use the concept of iteration
notes: Includes count-controlled loops, pre-condition loops, post-condition loops
items.detail:
Iteration typeCore idea
Count-controlledRepeats a specified number of times.
Pre-conditionCondition checked before the loop body.
Post-conditionCondition checked after the loop body.
items.svg: The three iteration forms

items.text: Understand and use the concepts of totalling and counting
items.detail:
TotallingMaintain and update a running total.
CountingMaintain and update a running count.

items.text: Understand and use the concept of string handling
notes: Includes: length, substring, upper, lower
The first character of a string can be position zero or one
items.detail:
RoutineWhat it does
LENGTHReturns string length.
SUBSTRINGGets a specified part of a string.
UCASEChanges letters to upper case.
LCASEChanges letters to lower case.

The first character can be position 0 or 1.

items.text: Understand and use arithmetic, relational and logical operators
notes: Arithmetic limited to: + − / * ^ MOD DIV
Relational limited to: = < <= > >= <>
Logical limited to: AND OR NOT
items.detail:
CategoryOperators in the syllabus
Arithmetic+ − / * ^ MOD DIV
Relational= < <= > >= <>
LogicalAND OR NOT

items.text: Understand and use nested statements
notes: Includes nested selection and iteration
Candidates will not be required to write more than three levels of nested statements
items.detail: Nested statements are selection or iteration structures placed inside another statement. The syllabus does not require more than three levels of nested statements.

items.text: Understand what is meant by procedures, functions and parameters, define and use them with or without parameters, and understand and use local and global variables
notes: Procedures and functions may have up to three parameters
items.detail:
TermWhat to know
ProcedureSubroutine used to carry out a task.
FunctionSubroutine that returns a value.
ParameterValue supplied to a procedure/function.
Local variableAvailable within the relevant procedure/function.
Global variableAvailable more widely in the program.

Procedures and functions can have up to three parameters.

items.text: Understand and use library routines
notes: Includes: MOD, DIV, ROUND, RANDOM
items.detail:
RoutineMeaning
MODRemainder after integer division.
DIVInteger quotient.
ROUNDRounds a number to the specified number of decimal places.
RANDOM()Returns a random number between 0 and 1 inclusive.

items.text: Understand how to create a maintainable program
notes: Includes appropriate use of meaningful identifiers, the commenting feature provided by the language, and procedures and functions
items.detail:
• use meaningful identifiers
  • use the language’s commenting feature appropriately
  • use procedures and functions appropriately

items.text: Declare and use one-dimensional (1D) and two-dimensional (2D) arrays
items.detail:
1D arrayUses one index to identify an element.
2D arrayUses two indices to identify an element.
items.svg: Arrays: one index vs two indexes

items.text: Understand the use of arrays
notes: Includes the use of variables as indexes in arrays
The first index can be zero or one
items.detail: Array indexes can be variables. The first index can be 0 or 1, so always match the index convention to the array declaration.

items.text: Write values into, and read values from, an array using iteration
notes: Includes nested iteration
items.detail: Use iteration to visit array elements when reading or writing values. For 2D arrays, nested iteration is used to visit the rows and columns.

items.text: Understand the purpose of storing data in a file to be used by a program
items.detail: Storing data in a file allows a program to use the data again rather than keeping it only during one execution of the program.

items.text: Open, close and use a file for reading and writing
notes: Includes read and write single items of data, and read and write a line of text
items.detail: The syllabus requires opening and closing a file and reading/writing single items of data and a line of text.

items.text: Define a single-table database from given data storage requirements
notes: Includes: fields, records, validation
items.detail:
TermMeaning
FieldA category of data in the table.
RecordA complete set of fields for one entry.
ValidationChecks that entered data follows the required rules.

items.text: Suggest suitable basic data types
notes: Includes: text/alphanumeric, character, Boolean, integer, real, date/time
items.detail:
Data typeUse for
Text/alphanumericLetters and numbers stored as text.
CharacterA single character.
BooleanTRUE/FALSE.
IntegerWhole numbers.
RealNumbers that can include a fractional part.
Date/timeDate or time values.

items.text: Understand the purpose of a primary key, and identify a suitable primary key for a given database table
keys: primary key for a given database table
items.detail: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in a table. When given a table, choose a field that uniquely identifies every record.

items.text: Read, understand and complete structured query language (SQL) scripts to query data stored in a single database table
notes: Limited to: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, ORDER BY DESCENDING, ORDER BY ASCENDING, SUM, COUNT, AND, OR
Identifying the output given by an SQL statement that will query the given contents of a database table
items.detail:
SQLPurpose in this syllabus
SELECTChoose fields to output.
FROMSpecify the table.
WHEREApply conditions.
ORDER BY ASCENDING / DESCENDINGSort results.
SUMCalculate a total.
COUNTCount records/values.
AND / ORCombine conditions.
items.svg: SQL: table → query

items.text: Identify and use the standard symbols for logic gates
notes: See section 4 of the syllabus for the standard logic gate symbols
items.detail: Know the standard symbols for NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR and XOR/EOR as shown in section 4 of the syllabus.
items.svg: Standard logic gate symbols

items.text: Define and understand the functions of logic gates
notes: Includes: NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR, XOR (EOR), and the binary output produced from all possible binary inputs
NOT is a single input gate; all other gates are limited to two inputs
items.detail:
ABANDORNANDNORXOR
0000110
0101101
1001101
1111000

NOT has one input: NOT 0 = 1 and NOT 1 = 0. Other gates are limited to two inputs.

items.text: Use logic gates to create circuits, complete truth tables, and write logic expressions, converting between a problem statement, a logic expression, a truth table and a logic circuit
keys: problem statement, a logic expression, a truth table and a logic circuit
notes: Circuits must be drawn for the statement given, without simplification
Logic circuits will be limited to a maximum of three inputs and one output
items.detail:
Three inputs → 8 truth-table rows
ABC
000
001
010
011
100
101
110
111

You may need to convert between a problem statement, logic expression, truth table and logic circuit. Do not simplify a circuit when the question requires it to be drawn from the given statement.
